semester1.cp: By the end of Semester 1, students will be able to recognize and use basic English vocabulary in everyday spoken contexts through play, songs, and stories; recognize letters A-N and their beginning sounds; and show growing confidence and enthusiasm in speaking English.
generalObjectives: Recognize and pronounce core vocabulary (greetings, body parts, colors, numbers, shapes, family, feelings) clearly.
Respond to simple English instructions and TPR movement cues.
Recognize and use basic sentence patterns orally (I am..., This is..., It is..., I feel...) without formal grammar explanations.
Recognize letters A-N and their beginning sounds through Alphabet Adventure and Phonics Detective.
Sing simple songs/chants and participate actively in play-based language games.
Build confidence, cooperation, and enjoyment in learning English.
semester1.grammarApproach: Because children are at the early-learner stage (ages 4-6), grammar is never taught as formal rules or terminology. Instead, one simple, repeatable sentence pattern per unit is instilled implicitly through play, songs, chants, TPR, and storytelling, gradually building the foundation for more structured grammar in Grade 1.

Sing new songs/chants and participate actively in games built around Semester 2 topics.
Build confidence, cooperation, and enjoyment in learning English, culminating in a Graduation Project showcase.

semester1.cp: By the end of Semester 1, students will be able to greet others and introduce themselves, name school objects and body parts, describe family members and home, identify colours and shapes, count and tell the time, and write simple sentences. They will master Alphabet A–Z phonics, short vowels, and CVC words, and perform a 1-minute 'All About Me' presentation.
generalObjectives: Greet others and introduce themselves using 'I am...' and 'My name is...'
Name and describe school objects, body parts, family members, rooms, colours, and shapes.
Use basic grammar patterns orally and in writing: I am / My name is / This is / These are / I have / There is/are / It is / Wh-questions.
Recognise and blend Alphabet A–Z, short vowels (a, e, i, o, u), and CVC words.
Read simple short passages and answer comprehension questions.
Write simple sentences independently and build growing vocabulary (target: 200–250 active words).
Build confidence, character, and enjoyment in learning English.
semester1.grammarApproach: Grammar is introduced implicitly through one repeatable sentence pattern per unit — practiced through chants, pair-work, games, and guided writing. No formal grammar terminology is used; patterns are drilled orally first, then transferred to reading and writing activities.

Quick recap of key vocabulary/grammar/phonics, one character-building reflection, and closing routine.

semester2.cp: By the end of Semester 2, students will be able to express food preferences, describe animal abilities, explain travel habits, talk about weather and clothing, narrate a daily routine, describe hobbies and sports, locate places in the neighborhood, and deliver a 2-minute 'My English Journey' final presentation. They will master beginning blends, digraphs, and sentence-reading fluency.
generalObjectives: Express likes/dislikes about food and animals using 'I like / I don't like' and 'can/can't'.
Describe how people travel using Simple Present (I go / She goes).
Describe weather and clothing using Present Continuous introduction (It is raining).
Narrate a daily routine using Simple Present + sequencing words (first, then, next, finally).
Talk about hobbies combining can/can't and I like/don't like.
Locate places using prepositions near, next to, between + there is/are review.
Deliver a 2-minute final 'My English Journey' presentation integrating all Grade 1 grammar.
Master beginning blends (bl, cl, fr, gr, sw, sl, sn, tr), digraphs (sh, ch, th, wh), and simple sentence reading fluency.
semester2.grammarApproach: Building on Semester 1 patterns, Semester 2 introduces more complex structures: Simple Present third person (goes/rides), Present Continuous (It is raining), and combined modal + preference patterns (can + I like). Each is introduced implicitly through chants, role plays, and guided writing.

overview.jumlahPertemuan: 18 Sessions (3 sessions per theme, once a week)
overview.fokusKeterampilan: Listening, Speaking, Reading & Writing — Foundational to Intermediate
overview.metode: Activity-Based, CLT, Songs & Chants, Games, Dialogue, Guided Writing
overview.mediaUtama: Flashcards, Audio, Worksheets, Realia, Illustrated Cards

semester1.cp: By the end of Semester 1, students will be able to greet and introduce themselves, use numbers and days in context, describe objects using color and shape, introduce family members, name body parts and express feelings, and name and describe animals — all using simple repeatable sentence patterns with growing confidence.
generalObjectives: Greet others and give a 2–3 sentence self-introduction including name and age.
Count and use numbers 1–20, name days of the week, and tell basic time.
Describe objects using color and shape in combined sentences.
Introduce family members using possessive adjectives and describe them simply.
Name body parts, respond to TPR instructions, and express feelings.
Name common animals, imitate their sounds, and describe them using simple adjectives.
Participate confidently in end-of-semester role plays and a short quiz.
semester1.grammarApproach: Grammar is introduced implicitly through one repeatable sentence pattern per theme. Each theme runs for 3 sessions: Session 1 introduces vocabulary and the sub-topic; Session 2 focuses on grammar and guided practice; Session 3 focuses on application, combined practice, and a short quiz. Patterns are drilled orally first, then transferred to reading and writing.

sessionStructure.deskripsi: Greeting, prayer, warm-up song or chant to build a positive mood.
Quick review of the previous session's vocabulary through Q&A, chants, or flashcards.
Introduce new vocabulary or grammar pattern using flashcards, songs, or realia.
Interactive games, role play, pair-work, or TPR activities to practice the new material.
Independent practice: worksheet, short writing, or dialogue task.
Recap the material, praise and reward students, closing greeting.

meetings.title: All About Me & Greetings — Vocabulary & Sub-Topic

meetings.grammarExample: Hello! Good morning. Thank you. Goodbye!

activities.deskripsi: Teacher greets the class warmly; students stick name tags on.

Introduce greeting flashcards (hello, goodbye, good morning, etc.) with listen & repeat drills.
Students practise greeting each other in pairs using the new expressions.
Tracing and colouring greeting words; matching greetings to time-of-day pictures.
Recap greeting words as a chant, short goodbye song.

assessment: Observation of pronunciation and confidence during Greeting Pairs.
Worksheet matching accuracy.

meetings.title: All About Me & Greetings — Grammar & Practice
objectives: Use 'I am / I'm + name' to introduce themselves.
Ask and answer 'What is your name?' and 'How old are you?'.
Introduce themselves in a 2–3 sentence spoken paragraph.
meetings.grammarPattern: I am / I'm + name or age
meetings.grammarExample: My name is Dimas. I am 8 years old. Nice to meet you.
meetings.grammarNote: 'I am' and 'I'm' introduced as equivalent forms for identity and age; practised through paired Q&A.

activities.deskripsi: Review greeting vocabulary through a quick ball-toss name game.

activities.kegiatan: Warm-up: Nice to Meet You Chant

Model 'I am ___ / I'm ___ years old' using a puppet and cue cards.
Students pair up with a different classmate each round and ask 'What is your name? / How old are you?'
Fill-in-the-blank: 'My name is ___. I am ___ years old.' Students draw a self-portrait.
A few volunteers share their self-portrait; closing greeting.

assessment: Fluency delivering the 2–3 sentence self-introduction.
Worksheet completeness and accuracy.

meetings.title: All About Me & Greetings — Application & Quiz
objectives: Combine greeting expressions and self-introduction into one connected spoken text.
Introduce themselves in a chain in front of the class.
Create a name card with a picture and a short self-introduction.
meetings.grammarPattern: Hello! My name is ___. I am ___ years old. Nice to meet you.
meetings.grammarExample: Hello! My name is Rani. I am 9 years old. Nice to meet you. Goodbye!
meetings.grammarNote: All greeting and identity patterns consolidated into one short spoken monologue.
vocab: review: hello, goodbye, name, age, nice to meet you, thank you

activities.deskripsi: Festive greeting; quick chant of all words learned in Sessions 1–2.

Students create a name card and present it using the full introduction pattern.
Oral quiz: teacher calls on each student to greet and introduce themselves. Written: match greeting to situation.
Collect name cards; give sticker rewards; closing greeting song.

assessment: Oral quiz: greeting + introduction fluency.
Name card completeness and written accuracy.

activities.deskripsi: Teacher shares a short story about their own family.
Singing 'Finger Family' while wiggling matching fingers.
Introduce the family tree poster; drill each family member word with flashcards.
Students role-play introducing their family using finger puppets.
Draw/label a simple family tree with the new vocabulary.
A few students share their family tree; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy naming family members during the puppet show.
Family tree worksheet completeness.

meetings.title: My Family — Grammar & Practice
objectives: Use possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her) correctly.

Write sentences describing family using photos or drawings.
meetings.grammarPattern: This is my ... / He/She is my ...
meetings.grammarExample: This is my mother. She is my mother. Her name is Siti.
meetings.grammarNote: 'My, your, his, her' introduced implicitly through family introduction sentences; 'This is my...' drilled as a fixed pattern.

Students interview a partner about their family using 'This is my __ / He/She is my __'.

Recap possessive adjectives with a quick matching quiz; closing greeting.

assessment: Correct use of possessive adjectives in speech.
Worksheet sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: My Family — Application & Quiz

Draw a family tree and present it to the class.
Answer a short oral and written quiz about family vocabulary and patterns.
meetings.grammarPattern: This is my ___. His/Her name is ___. He/She is ___.
meetings.grammarExample: This is my family. This is my father. His name is Budi. He is kind.
meetings.grammarNote: All family patterns consolidated into a short description — students produce 3–4 connected sentences independently.

Written quiz: matching and sentence accuracy.

Worksheet accuracy: number words and day ordering.

meetings.title: Numbers, Days & Time — Grammar & Practice

Worksheet accuracy: time writing and day fill-in.

Imitate animal sounds correctly.
Identify animals from pictures and audio sound clips.
meetings.grammarExample: This is a cat. The cat says meow.
meetings.grammarNote: Animal vocabulary introduced through sound guessing, flashcards, and the animal-sound pattern.

activities.deskripsi: Guess-the-sound warm-up using an audio clip of different animals.
Singing 'Old MacDonald Had a Farm' with animal sounds.
Introduce animal flashcards paired with sounds; drill 'The ___ says ___'.
Students wear simple masks and act out the animal's sound and movement.
Match animals to their names and sounds; circle the correct animal from audio clue descriptions.
Recap animal names and sounds as a class chant; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy imitating and naming animals.
Matching worksheet accuracy.

meetings.title: Animals Around Us — Grammar & Practice
objectives: Use 'There is / There are + animal' to describe quantities.
Form simple plural nouns by adding +s.
Use 'can' to describe animal abilities: 'Can a bird fly?'
meetings.grammarExample: There are three rabbits. A bird can fly. A fish cannot walk.
meetings.grammarNote: 'There is/are' for existence and 'can' for ability introduced through a wildlife poster activity; plural +s practised with animal counting.

activities.deskripsi: Quick animal name review from Session 13 using flashcard flip.
Chanting 'There is one cat / There are two dogs' with finger counting.
Teach 'there is/are + plural' using picture cards; teach 'can/cannot' for animal abilities.
Teams sort animal cards into singular/plural; then answer 'Can a ___ ___?' in a quiz game.
Write 'There is/are ___'; complete 'A ___ can ___ / A ___ cannot ___'.
Recap 'can' sentences with a quick round of oral Q&A; closing greeting.

assessment: Correct use of 'there is/are' and 'can/cannot' in speech.
Worksheet singular/plural and sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Animals Around Us — Application & Quiz
objectives: Describe an animal using its name, sound, size, and ability in 2–3 sentences.
Participate in an animal mask role play.
Complete an oral and written quiz on animal vocabulary and grammar.
meetings.grammarPattern: This is a ___. It can ___. There are ___ ___s.
meetings.grammarExample: This is a rabbit. It is small. It can jump. There are five rabbits in the field.
meetings.grammarNote: All animal patterns consolidated; students produce a 3-sentence animal description independently.
vocab: review: cat, dog, bird, fish, cow, chicken, duck, rabbit, elephant, lion, can, there is, there are

activities.deskripsi: Singing Old MacDonald as a class for fun review.
Teacher gives clues: 'It is big. It is grey. It can swim.' Students guess the animal.
Model a full 3-sentence animal description; class repeats.
Students wear masks, act out their animal, and describe it to classmates.
Oral: describe one animal in 2–3 sentences. Written: fill in 'can/cannot', 'there is/are', and name the animal from a picture.
Display drawings; give sticker rewards; closing greeting.

assessment: Oral description: 3-sentence animal description.
Written quiz: 'can', 'there is/are', and vocabulary accuracy.

meetings.title: My Classroom & School Things — Vocabulary & Sub-Topic
objectives: Name common classroom objects: book, pencil, eraser, ruler, bag, chair, table, blackboard, teacher, student.
Point to and say each object in the real classroom.
Participate in a classroom object listen-and-repeat activity.
meetings.grammarPattern: This is a ___. / I have a ___.
meetings.grammarExample: This is my book. I have a pencil in my bag.
meetings.grammarNote: Classroom vocabulary introduced using real objects before prepositions and 'where' questions are built in Session 17.

activities.deskripsi: Teacher points to classroom objects and asks 'What is this?'
Chanting classroom object names while pointing to the real items.
Introduce object flashcards with listen & repeat; drill pronunciation.
Teacher calls an object name; students touch the real object first and win a point.
Match classroom objects to their names; draw and label three objects in their own bag.
Recap object names; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy naming classroom objects in the Touch and Name Game.
Matching worksheet accuracy.

meetings.title: My Classroom & School Things — Grammar & Practice
objectives: Use 'This/These is/are ...' to describe singular and plural classroom objects.
Use prepositions of place: in, on, under.
Ask and answer 'Where is my ___?'
meetings.grammarPattern: This/These is/are ... / Where is the ___? It is in/on/under the ___.
meetings.grammarExample: This is my pencil. These are my books. Where is my eraser? It is on the table.
meetings.grammarNote: 'This/these' for singular/plural and 'in/on/under' prepositions introduced together through a hide-and-find game.

activities.deskripsi: Quick review of classroom objects from Session 16 via flashcard flash.
Chanting 'Where is the pencil? It is on the table' with actions.
Teach 'This/These is/are' for singular/plural; teach prepositions 'in, on, under' using real objects.
Teacher hides an object; students ask 'Where is the ___?' and answer 'It is in/on/under the ___.
Circle 'This/These'; fill in prepositions; draw an object in/on/under a box.
Rapid-fire 'Where is the ___?' Q&A with real objects; closing greeting.

assessment: Correct use of 'This/These' and prepositions in speech.
Worksheet fill-in accuracy.

meetings.title: My Classroom & School Things — Application, Review & End-of-Semester Quiz
objectives: Apply all Semester 1 vocabulary and grammar patterns in a combined review game.
Describe classroom object locations using prepositions.
Complete a written end-of-semester evaluation and a short oral quiz.
meetings.grammarPattern: Where is my ___? It is in/on/under the ___. These are my ___s.
meetings.grammarExample: Where is my pencil? It is on the table. These are my books. They are in my bag.
meetings.grammarNote: Session 18 doubles as the Semester 1 end-of-term review: classroom theme + cumulative vocabulary and grammar from all 6 themes.
vocab: review: all Semester 1 themes — greetings, family, numbers/days/time, body/feelings, animals, classroom objects

activities.deskripsi: Festive greeting; quick chant medley of songs from all 6 themes.
Teams race to correctly name flashcards from all six Semester 1 themes.
Combined classroom + preposition game: students hide objects and use 'Where is/are the ___? It is ___'.
Team quiz covering all Semester 1 grammar patterns: greetings, family, numbers, body, animals, classroom.
Written worksheet: match, fill-in, and short sentence writing covering all 6 themes.
Announce scores; praise and reward all students; closing semester greeting.

assessment: Team quiz performance across all Semester 1 themes.
End-of-semester worksheet accuracy.

overview.jumlahPertemuan: 18 Sessions (3 sessions per theme + 3 review sessions, once a week)
overview.fokusKeterampilan: Listening, Speaking, Reading & Writing — Intermediate Vocabulary & Grammar
overview.metode: Activity-Based, CLT, Songs & Chants, Games, Dialogue, Role Play
overview.mediaUtama: Flashcards, Audio, Worksheets, Realia, Illustrated Cards, Simple Props

semester2.cp: By the end of Semester 2, students will be able to name and classify land and water transport, discuss halal and haram food, interact in a shopping role play, describe appropriate Islamic dress, and talk about professions — all using grammar structures including homophones, irregular plurals, compound words, irregular verbs, contractions, adjectives/adverbs, and silent-letter spelling patterns.
generalObjectives: Classify types of transportation and use them in sentences about journeys.
Discuss lawful and forbidden food using appropriate vocabulary and Islamic values.
Role-play a buying-and-selling scenario using polite language and honesty.
Describe Islamic dress using modest clothing vocabulary and appropriate adjectives.
Name and talk about various professions, including the role of writers.
Use grammar: homophones, irregular plurals, compound words, irregular verbs, contractions, adjectives/adverbs, silent kn/wr spellings, soft G, and commas.
Demonstrate character values: gratitude in travel, choosing halal food, honest trade, modest dress, and writing as a means of sharing goodness.
semester2.grammarApproach: Semester 2 introduces named grammar points explicitly (homophones, irregular plurals, compound words, etc.) while continuing the 3-session-per-theme pattern. Session 1 covers vocabulary and context; Session 2 targets grammar explicitly with worksheet practice; Session 3 integrates character building, combined practice, and a short quiz. The final three sessions (16–18) review all themes through games and a group final project.

sessionStructure.deskripsi: Greeting, prayer, warm-up song or chant to build a positive mood.
Quick review of the previous session's vocabulary through Q&A, chants, or flashcards.
Introduce new vocabulary or grammar point using flashcards, songs, or board examples.
Interactive games, role play, pair-work, or TPR activities to practise the new material.
Independent practice: worksheet, short writing, or dialogue task.
Recap the material, praise and reward students, closing greeting.

meetings.title: Transportation — Vocabulary: Land vs. Water Transport
objectives: Name and classify land transport: car, bus, motorcycle, bicycle, train, truck.
Name and classify water transport: ship, boat, sail.
Sort transport picture cards into land vs. water categories.
Listen and repeat transport vocabulary with correct pronunciation.
meetings.grammarPattern: I go by ___. / A ___ travels on land/water.
meetings.grammarExample: I go to school by bus. A ship travels on water.
meetings.grammarNote: Transport vocabulary introduced through picture card classification; grammar patterns introduced naturally through sorting activity.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting; teacher asks 'How did you come to school today?'
Chanting transport words with matching movement gestures (drive, sail, ride).
Introduce transport flashcards; sort them into land vs. water on a poster.
Teams race to correctly place transport cards into 'Land' or 'Water' columns.
Circle land transport in one colour; water transport in another; write the name of each vehicle.
Recap vocabulary; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy classifying transport in the card game.
Worksheet labelling accuracy.

meetings.title: Transportation — Grammar: Homophones & Irregular Plurals
objectives: Recognise and use homophones in context: sail/sale, sea/see, road/rode, buy/by, way/weigh.
Form irregular plural nouns: man→men, person→people, child→children.
Practise with a homophone matching game and irregular plural worksheet.
meetings.grammarPattern: sail ≠ sale; sea ≠ see / man → men, child → children
meetings.grammarExample: We sail on the sea. The children ride the bus. Two men drove the truck.
meetings.grammarNote: Homophones (same sound, different meaning/spelling) and irregular plurals introduced explicitly through games and board examples.

activities.deskripsi: Review transport vocabulary from Session 1 with a quick flashcard flip.
Teacher writes 'sail/sale' on the board and shows both pictures; class discusses the difference.
Teach all five homophone pairs with visual examples; then teach irregular plurals (man/men, person/people, child/children).

activities.kegiatan: Practice: Homophone Match + Irregular Plural Sort
activities.deskripsi: Match homophone cards to pictures; then form irregular plural sentences from prompt cards.
Choose the correct homophone in sentences; write irregular plural forms.
Quick oral drill: teacher says a word, students give the homophone; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy choosing correct homophones in context.
Irregular plural worksheet accuracy.

meetings.title: Transportation — Character Building & Application Quiz
objectives: Memorise and practise the prayer for riding a vehicle (doa safar).
Express gratitude and safety awareness during travel as a character value.
Create a mini journey map using transport and destination vocabulary.
Complete a short oral and written quiz on transport vocabulary and grammar.
meetings.grammarPattern: I am going to ___ by ___. The ___ travels on ___.
meetings.grammarExample: I am going to Jakarta by train. Many people ride the bus. The children walk to school.
meetings.grammarNote: Transport vocabulary, homophones, and irregular plurals applied in a combined journey context; doa safar introduced as a meaningful cultural-religious element.
vocab: review: car, bus, ship, train, homophones, men/people/children, journey, map, destination

activities.deskripsi: Class recites the doa safar together; teacher explains its meaning briefly.
Short discussion: 'Why should we be grateful when travelling safely?'
Students draw a simple journey map using transport and destination vocabulary; label using learned vocab.
Each student describes their journey map to a partner: 'I am going to ___ by ___.'
Oral: name three vehicles, give the irregular plural of 'child', match one homophone pair. Written: fill-in sentences.
Display journey maps; doa safar recap; closing greeting.

assessment: Journey map presentation: vocabulary and sentence accuracy.
Quiz: homophones, irregular plurals, and transport vocabulary.

meetings.title: Food — Vocabulary: Halal & Haram Foods
objectives: Name and classify halal and haram food items.
Use vocabulary: halal, haram, pork, alcohol, meat, pure, clean, forbidden, allowed, fish, vegetable, fruit.
Sort food picture cards into halal vs. haram categories.
meetings.grammarPattern: This food is halal / haram. / We are allowed / not allowed to eat ___.
meetings.grammarExample: Fish is halal. Pork is haram. We are not allowed to eat pork.
meetings.grammarNote: Halal/haram food vocabulary introduced through picture sorting; moral framing kept positive and educational.

activities.deskripsi: Teacher asks 'What did you eat for breakfast today?' — students answer in English.
Chanting food names (rice, fish, fruit, vegetable) with pointing gestures.
Introduce halal/haram concept with picture cards; sort into allowed/forbidden categories on the poster.

activities.kegiatan: Practice: Halal or Haram? Sorting Game
activities.deskripsi: Teams race to place food cards into the correct column; discuss their choices.
Circle halal foods; cross out haram ones; complete: 'This is ___ food. It is ___.
Recap vocabulary; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy in halal/haram sorting game.
Worksheet sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Food — Grammar: Compound Words & Irregular Verbs
objectives: Identify and use compound words: breakfast, seafood, cupcake, sunflower, notebook.
Learn irregular verb forms: eat–ate–eaten, drink–drank–drunk, buy–bought–bought, give–gave–given.
Use irregular verbs in simple sentences about food.
meetings.grammarPattern: I ate ___ for breakfast. / She bought ___ at the market.
meetings.grammarExample: Yesterday I ate rice and fish for breakfast. We bought cupcakes at the bakery. She drank milk.
meetings.grammarNote: Compound words introduced as two words joined into one; irregular verbs taught as base/past sets with focus on past tense form in context.

activities.deskripsi: Review food vocabulary and halal/haram sorting from Session 4.
Teacher shows 'break' + 'fast' → 'breakfast'; students guess other compound words.
Teach five compound words; then introduce irregular verb sets with a table on the board.

activities.kegiatan: Practice: Compound Word Building + Verb Game
activities.deskripsi: Build compound words from half-cards; then play a 'Change the Verb!' relay with irregular forms.
Join word halves to make compound words; fill in past tense forms of irregular verbs in sentences.
Quick irregular verb drill (teacher says base, students say past); closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy building compound words.
Worksheet irregular verb form accuracy.

meetings.title: Food — Character Building & Application Quiz
objectives: Discuss the importance of choosing halal and tayyib (wholesome) food as Islamic character.
Complete a halal food stall role play using compound words and irregular verbs.
Complete a short oral and written quiz on food vocabulary and grammar.
meetings.grammarPattern: Yesterday I ate ___. I always buy ___ food. Eating halal is ___.
meetings.grammarExample: Yesterday I ate seafood for breakfast. I always buy halal food. Eating halal food is important for our health.
meetings.grammarNote: All food-theme grammar consolidated: compound words and irregular verbs used in sentences that reflect halal food choices and Islamic values.
vocab: review: halal, haram, breakfast, seafood, cupcake, eat/ate, drink/drank, buy/bought, give/gave

activities.deskripsi: Class discussion: 'What does tayyib mean? Why should food be clean and good?'
Students share one halal food they love; teacher connects to Islamic values of purity.
Sort food cards and build sentences using compound words and irregular verbs.
Students role-play a halal food stall: seller offers food, buyer uses irregular verbs ('I bought rice and fish.').
Oral: describe what you ate yesterday using irregular verbs. Written: compound words and irregular verb fill-in.
Recap values; adab makan reminder; closing greeting.

assessment: Role play: correct use of irregular verbs in food context.
Quiz: compound words and irregular verbs accuracy.

meetings.title: Shopping — Vocabulary: Traditional & Modern Markets
objectives: Name shopping vocabulary: seller, buyer, price, bargain, market, supermarket, stall, goods.
Compare traditional market and modern market in simple English.
Use shopping vocabulary in a brief discussion.
meetings.grammarPattern: I buy ___ at the ___. / The price is ___.
meetings.grammarExample: I buy vegetables at the traditional market. The price is cheap. I bargain with the seller.
meetings.grammarNote: Shopping vocabulary introduced through picture comparison of traditional vs. modern markets before grammar focus in Session 8.

activities.deskripsi: Teacher asks 'Where does your family buy food?'
Compare a traditional market picture with a supermarket picture; name what you see.
Introduce shopping vocabulary flashcards; model key sentences using play money.
Students role-play buying and selling using shopping vocabulary; use play money.
Label market pictures; complete sentences: 'The seller sells ___ at the ___.
Recap shopping vocabulary; closing greeting.

assessment: Vocabulary accuracy in the pretend market.
Worksheet labelling and sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Shopping — Grammar: Contractions & Adjectives/Adverbs
objectives: Form and use contractions: don't, can't, isn't, it's, I'm, won't.
Distinguish and use adjectives and adverbs: cheap/cheaply, honest/honestly, quick/quickly.
Practise contractions in shopping dialogues.
meetings.grammarPattern: I don't want ___. / She sells cheaply. / He is honest.
meetings.grammarExample: I don't want that. It isn't fresh. She sells vegetables cheaply. He is an honest seller.
meetings.grammarNote: Contractions introduced as shortened spoken forms; adjectives/adverbs distinguished through shopping context (cheap→cheaply describes how something is done).

activities.deskripsi: Review shopping vocabulary from Session 7 with a quick Q&A.
Teacher writes 'do not → don't'; students guess other contractions.
Teach six contractions with full-form pairs; then teach adjective→adverb transformation in shopping sentences.
Rewrite full-form sentences into contractions; then sort adjective/adverb cards into correct columns.
Rewrite sentences using contractions; fill in the correct adjective or adverb form.
Oral drill: teacher says full form, students say contraction; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy writing contractions.
Adjective/adverb worksheet accuracy.

meetings.title: Shopping — Character Building & Application Quiz
objectives: Discuss Islamic principles of honest and ethical trading (jujur, ridha sama ridha).
Role-play a market buying-and-selling scene using contractions and adverbs.
Complete a short oral and written quiz on shopping vocabulary and grammar.
meetings.grammarPattern: I don't want ___. / She sells ___ cheaply and honestly.
meetings.grammarExample: I don't want pork. I'm looking for halal food. She sells fish cheaply and honestly. Can't you give a better price?
meetings.grammarNote: Shopping role play integrates contractions and adjectives/adverbs while reinforcing honest trade as an Islamic value.
vocab: review: seller, buyer, market, price, bargain, don't, can't, isn't, cheap/cheaply, honest/honestly
media: Role play props (play money, stall sign)

activities.deskripsi: Character discussion: 'What makes a good seller? What makes a good buyer?'
Briefly introduce 'jujur (honest)' and 'ridha sama ridha (mutual agreement)' in simple terms.
Full buying-and-selling role play using contractions: 'I don't want that / It isn't fresh / I'm buying vegetables.'
Students describe how their market character acts: 'The seller speaks honestly. She works quickly.'
Oral: use one contraction and one adverb in a market sentence. Written: contraction rewrite and adjective/adverb fill-in.
Recap honest trading values; closing greeting.

assessment: Role play: correct contraction and adverb use.
Quiz: contraction and adjective/adverb accuracy.

meetings.title: Clothes — Vocabulary: Islamic Dress
objectives: Name Islamic clothing vocabulary: hijab, headscarf, modest, cover, aurat, robe, loose, neat, clean, simple.
Discuss the concept of modest dress in simple English.
Listen and repeat clothing vocabulary with correct pronunciation.
meetings.grammarPattern: I wear ___ / She is wearing ___. / Muslim clothing is ___.
meetings.grammarExample: I wear a hijab to cover my hair. Muslim clothing is modest and clean.
meetings.grammarNote: Islamic dress vocabulary introduced descriptively and respectfully through picture discussion before grammar in Session 11.

activities.deskripsi: Teacher asks 'What are you wearing today?'
Chanting clothing words with matching actions (cover head, tie, button).
Introduce Islamic clothing vocabulary using picture cards; discuss what each word means.
Students look at clothing pictures and describe them: 'She is wearing a loose robe. It is modest and clean.'
Match clothing words to pictures; complete: 'Muslim clothing is ___ and ___.
Recap clothing vocabulary; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy naming and describing clothing items.
Worksheet match and sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Clothes — Grammar: Silent Letters (kn/wr) & Advanced Prepositions
objectives: Spell and pronounce silent-letter words: know, knee, knife, knock, knit; write, wrist, wrong, wrap.
Use advanced prepositions of place: in front of, behind, between, next to, over.
Locate people and objects using the new prepositions.
meetings.grammarPattern: kn = /n/; wr = /r/ / The ___ is in front of / behind / next to ___.
meetings.grammarExample: I know how to knit. The bag is next to the door. The scarf is wrapped over her shoulders.
meetings.grammarNote: Silent-letter spelling rules taught explicitly with pronunciation; prepositions extended beyond in/on/under to in front of, behind, between, next to, over.

activities.deskripsi: Review clothing vocabulary from Session 10.
Teacher writes 'know' and asks 'Do you hear the K?' Explore why some letters are silent.
Teach kn/wr silent letters with card drills; then teach 5 new prepositions using classroom object demonstrations.

activities.kegiatan: Practice: Silent Letter Cards + Preposition Relay
activities.deskripsi: Spell and say silent-letter words from cards; place real objects and describe their location using new prepositions.
Circle the silent letter in kn/wr words; fill in prepositions in picture sentences.
Quick oral drill: teacher holds up a word, students pronounce it; closing greeting.

assessment: Correct pronunciation and spelling of kn/wr words.
Preposition worksheet fill-in accuracy.

meetings.title: Clothes — Character Building & Application Quiz
objectives: Discuss the etiquette of dressing and the Sunnah guidelines on modest clothing.
Combine Islamic dress vocabulary, kn/wr spelling, and prepositions in a description task.
Complete a short oral and written quiz on clothing vocabulary and grammar.
meetings.grammarPattern: She is wearing a ___ in front of / next to ___. I know that ___ is wrong.
meetings.grammarExample: She is wearing a loose robe. Her bag is next to her. I know that wearing clean clothes is right. It is wrong to dress improperly.
meetings.grammarNote: Clothing theme consolidated with silent-letter words and prepositions applied in a descriptive context aligned with Islamic values of modesty.
vocab: review: hijab, modest, loose, neat, know, knee, write, wrap, in front of, behind, between, next to, over

activities.deskripsi: Discussion: 'Why do Muslims dress modestly? What does the Sunnah say?'
Students describe a picture using clothing vocabulary and prepositions: 'The hijab is next to the mirror. She wraps it over her head.'
Spelling bee with kn/wr words in a clothing context ('She knows how to knit a scarf.').
Students dress a paper doll in modest clothing and describe their choices aloud.
Oral: describe one piece of clothing using a preposition. Written: kn/wr spelling and preposition fill-in.
Recap Islamic dress values; closing greeting.

assessment: Clothing description: vocabulary and preposition accuracy.
Quiz: kn/wr spelling and preposition fill-in.

meetings.title: Professions — Vocabulary & Sub-Topic
objectives: Name and describe professions: writer, author, journalist, editor, engineer.
Recognise profession-related vocabulary: publish, story, imagine.
Identify professions from pictures and tool-of-the-trade clue cards.
meetings.grammarPattern: A ___ writes / builds / designs ___. / She is a ___.
meetings.grammarExample: A writer writes stories. An engineer builds bridges. She is a journalist.
meetings.grammarNote: Profession vocabulary introduced through picture guessing and tool-of-the-trade clues before grammar in Session 14.

activities.deskripsi: Teacher asks 'What do you want to be when you grow up?'
Students act out or hold a prop representing a profession; classmates guess.
Introduce profession flashcards with listen & repeat; model 'A ___ is a person who ___.
Teacher gives clues ('This person writes news stories for a newspaper.'); students guess the profession.
Match professions to their descriptions; complete: 'A writer ___. An engineer ___.
Recap profession vocabulary; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy guessing and naming professions.
Worksheet matching and sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Professions — Grammar: Soft G & Commas
objectives: Recognise and pronounce soft G words: giant, gym, giraffe, orange, engineer, magic, imagine.
Use commas correctly in lists, dates, and addresses.
Practise both grammar points in profession-themed sentences.
meetings.grammarPattern: g before e/i/y = /dʒ/ / Comma in lists: A, B, and C.
meetings.grammarExample: A journalist, an editor, and an engineer work at the same company. Imagine a giant giraffe at the gym!
meetings.grammarNote: Soft G rule taught with examples from profession vocabulary; commas in lists introduced using profession-themed sentences.

activities.deskripsi: Review profession vocabulary from Session 13.
Teacher writes 'go/get' (hard G) vs. 'giraffe/gym' (soft G); students hear and feel the difference.
Teach soft G rule with examples; then teach comma use in lists, dates, and addresses.

activities.kegiatan: Practice: Soft G Card Sort + Comma Insertion
activities.deskripsi: Sort G-words into hard/soft columns; insert missing commas in profession-themed sentences.
Mark hard/soft G; add commas to given sentences in a profession context.
Quick oral drill: say a G word and identify soft/hard; closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy identifying and pronouncing soft G words.
Comma insertion worksheet accuracy.

meetings.title: Professions — 'Become a Writer' & Character Building Quiz
objectives: Understand writing as a means of sharing goodness (character value).
Write a short simple story or descriptive paragraph in a mini writer's workshop.
Complete a quiz on profession vocabulary, soft G, and commas.
meetings.grammarPattern: I am a writer. I imagine ___. I write stories about ___.
meetings.grammarExample: I am a young writer. I imagine a giant giraffe at the zoo. I write stories about animals and nature. A writer, a journalist, and an editor all love words.
meetings.grammarNote: Profession theme concluded with a character-building mini project: students write a short story using profession vocabulary, soft G words, and commas.
vocab: review: writer, author, journalist, editor, engineer, giant, gym, giraffe, imagine, publish

activities.deskripsi: Discussion: 'How can a writer share goodness with the world?'
Students brainstorm positive things they could write about (kindness, nature, family).
Each student writes a 3–5 sentence story or description including at least one soft G word and one comma-in-list.
Volunteers read their story aloud; class gives simple positive feedback.
Oral: name three professions. Written: soft G identification, comma insertion, and one sentence about a profession.
Display stories; encourage future writing; closing greeting.

assessment: Mini story: vocabulary range, soft G usage, and comma placement.
Quiz: profession vocabulary, soft G, and commas.

meetings.title: Review & Final Project — Vocabulary Review (All Semester 2 Themes)
objectives: Review vocabulary from all five Semester 2 themes: Transportation, Food, Shopping, Clothes, Professions.
Participate in a combined vocabulary guessing game.
Begin preparing for the end-of-year role play project: 'A Day at the Market'.
meetings.grammarPattern: Review of all Semester 2 sentence patterns.
meetings.grammarExample: I go to the market by bus. I buy halal food. The seller sells vegetables cheaply. I am wearing a hijab. The editor works at a big company.
meetings.grammarNote: Session 16 is a vocabulary-focused review using games; no new grammar introduced. Groups are assigned roles for the final project.
vocab: All Semester 2 vocabulary: transport, food (halal/haram), shopping, clothing, professions
media: Mixed vocabulary flashcards from all themes

activities.deskripsi: Festive greeting; quick vocabulary song medley from Semester 2 themes.
Teams race to name mixed vocabulary flashcards from all five themes.
Students give clues in English for teammates to guess the word from any Semester 2 theme.
Introduce the 'A Day at the Market' role play project; assign groups and roles (seller, buyer, traveller, professional).
Groups brainstorm their role play script using vocabulary from their assigned themes.
Recap vocabulary categories; closing greeting.

assessment: Vocabulary guessing game participation.
Project planning engagement and vocabulary use.

meetings.title: Review & Final Project — Grammar Review (All Semester 2 Grammar)
objectives: Review all Semester 2 grammar points: homophones, irregular plurals, compound words, irregular verbs, contractions, adjectives/adverbs, kn/wr spelling, soft G, commas.
Complete a mixed grammar practice worksheet.
Rehearse the 'A Day at the Market' role play with teacher feedback.
meetings.grammarExample: The children rode the bus (irregular plural + homophone). I don't eat pork (contraction). She sells vegetables cheaply (adjective/adverb). I know the engineer (silent kn).
meetings.grammarNote: Session 17 consolidates all grammar points through a mixed drill worksheet and role play rehearsal; teacher identifies common errors for correction.

activities.deskripsi: Quick grammar recall: teacher reads a sentence, students identify the grammar point.
Teams answer rapid-fire grammar questions covering all Semester 2 points.
Students complete a mixed worksheet: homophones, irregular plurals, compound words, contractions, adverbs, kn/wr, soft G, commas.
Groups rehearse their 'A Day at the Market' role play; teacher gives grammar and vocabulary feedback.
Teacher presents common errors on the board; students correct them together.
Final encouragement before the showcase; closing greeting.

assessment: Mixed grammar worksheet accuracy across all grammar points.
Role play rehearsal observation: grammar and vocabulary use.

meetings.title: Review & Final Project — 'A Day at the Market' Showcase & Final Evaluation
objectives: Perform the 'A Day at the Market' group role play combining all five Semester 2 themes.
Use transport, food, shopping, clothing, and profession vocabulary in one connected performance.
Complete the final written and oral evaluation for the full year.
meetings.grammarPattern: All Semester 2 grammar integrated in the role play.
meetings.grammarExample: We came to the market by train. I don't want pork — I only buy halal food. The seller sells vegetables cheaply and honestly. The journalist writes about the market. I wear my hijab. The children and I had a great day!
meetings.grammarNote: Final capstone task: students integrate transport, food, shopping, clothing, and profession knowledge in one connected group performance demonstrating the year's grammar and character values.
vocab: All Semester 2 vocabulary — transport, food, shopping, clothes, professions
media: Role play props (play money, stall sign, transport card, clothing)

activities.deskripsi: Festive final greeting; class recites doa safar one last time.
Quick last run of vocabulary from all five themes using flashcard relay.

activities.kegiatan: 'A Day at the Market' Group Performance
activities.deskripsi: Each group performs their role play in front of the class; audience gives simple positive feedback.
Teacher calls on individual students for oral questions covering vocabulary, grammar, and values from the whole year.
Written test: vocabulary matching, grammar fill-in (all Semester 2 points), and a 2–3 sentence short writing task.
Award certificates; group photo; year-end reflection; closing song.

assessment: Role play performance: vocabulary range, grammar accuracy, confidence, and team collaboration.
Oral evaluation: vocabulary, grammar, and character values.
Written final evaluation: comprehensive accuracy across all Semester 2 grammar points.

semester1.cp: By the end of Semester 1, students will be able to introduce themselves in detail, use adverbs of frequency and precise time expressions, describe schedules and professions, describe locations and directions in town, express ability and obligation using modals, and compare people/objects using comparative adjectives.
generalObjectives: Give a detailed self-introduction including reasons for preferences.
Use adverbs of frequency and tell precise time using past/to.
Describe a weekly schedule and ask about jobs/professions.
Describe locations and give simple directions using prepositions.
Use can/can't and must/mustn't to express ability and obligation.
Form and use comparative adjectives to compare two people or objects.
semester1.grammarApproach: Students already master simple present, simple past, and regular/plural nouns, so those are only briefly reviewed as a diagnostic in Week 2. Class time is redirected to new, more challenging structures: adverbs of frequency, modals (can/must), present continuous vs simple present, comparatives & superlatives, conjunctions, and simple future (going to) - each introduced explicitly as a named grammar point, practiced, then produced in speaking or writing.

sessionStructure.deskripsi: Greeting and warm-up question related to the day's topic.
Quick review of the previous session's material or vocabulary.
Explicit introduction of the new grammar point/vocabulary with examples on the board.
Guided speaking/writing practice, games, or roleplay using the new structure.
Independent application: short writing, worksheet, or speaking task.
Recap the grammar point, assign light homework if needed, closing greeting.

petaMateri.grammar: I am / I live in / I am... years old

petaMateri.kosakata: bus, car, go straight, turn left/right
petaMateri.grammar: How do you go to school?

meetings.title: All About Me (Full Version)
objectives: Students can present themselves in more detail, including age, address, and hobby.
Students can give a simple reason for a preference using "because".
meetings.grammarPattern: I am... / I live in... / I am ... years old.
meetings.grammarExample: I like drawing because it is fun.
meetings.grammarNote: Reviewing familiar self-introduction patterns while adding a reason clause with "because" as a light preview.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, quick icebreaker asking students their names and one hobby.
Students act out a hobby for classmates to guess.
Model a fuller self-introduction: name, age, address, hobby, and reason.
Students prepare and present a 4-5 sentence self-introduction to a partner.
Writing their own detailed self-introduction paragraph.
A few volunteers present to the class, closing greeting.

assessment: Fluency and detail in the self-introduction.
Written paragraph completeness and accuracy.

meetings.title: Quick Review: Present & Past Tense
objectives: Students can correctly distinguish simple present and simple past tense in mixed sentences.
Teacher can identify each student's current grammar level for planning purposes.
meetings.grammarExample: She plays every day. / She played yesterday.
meetings.grammarNote: A diagnostic review, not new material - used to map each student's actual ability since "already studied" can mean very different levels.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, explain today is a fun review/check-up day.
Teacher reads random sentences; students shout "present" or "past".
Briefly recap the two tenses using timeline visuals (now vs. yesterday).
Students sort scrambled sentence cards into "Present" and "Past" piles in teams.
A short diagnostic worksheet mixing present/past sentences for the teacher to assess levels.
Recap common mistakes noticed, closing greeting.

assessment: Diagnostic worksheet used to map each student's grammar level.
Accuracy sorting sentences by tense.

meetings.title: Adverbs of Frequency
objectives: Students can use adverbs of frequency correctly with simple present tense.
Students can describe their own daily routine using frequency words.
meetings.grammarExample: I always brush my teeth. I never eat vegetables.
meetings.grammarNote: Explicitly introducing frequency adverbs (always, usually, sometimes, never) and their position before the main verb.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask students how often they do a sample activity.
Students physically line up from "always" to "never" based on a habit.
Explain frequency adverbs and their placement in a sentence, with example sentences on the board.
Students describe their daily routine to a partner using at least 3 frequency words.
Writing 5 sentences about their routine using different frequency adverbs.
A few students share one sentence, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct placement of frequency adverbs in speech.
Written sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Telling Time (Advanced)
objectives: Students can read precise clock times including minutes.
Students can use "past" and "to" correctly when telling time.
meetings.grammarExample: It's twenty past seven. It's a quarter to nine.
meetings.grammarNote: Extending basic time-telling to precise minute expressions using past/to, a common area of confusion.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask what time it is right now.
Quick review of telling time on the hour and half hour.
Explain "past" and "to" with several clock examples on the board.
In pairs, students set a practice clock to a time the teacher calls out.
Reading and writing 6 clock times using past/to correctly.
Recap the past/to rule, closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy setting the clock to called-out times.
Worksheet accuracy reading/writing times.

meetings.title: My Schedule & Timetable
objectives: Students can describe their weekly school schedule.
Students can write a short paragraph combining time, frequency, and subjects.
meetings.grammarExample: I have Math class at 8 o'clock. I always study English on Monday.
meetings.grammarNote: Combining the previous three weeks' structures (present tense, frequency, time) into connected writing.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask what subject they have today.
Matching subject names to related pictures.
Model describing a sample timetable using time + frequency + subject.
Students interview a partner about their weekly schedule.
Writing a short paragraph describing their own daily/weekly timetable.
A few students share one line from their timetable, closing greeting.

assessment: Fluency describing the timetable orally.
Paragraph writing accuracy and structure.

meetings.title: Jobs & Professions
objectives: Students can name common jobs/professions in English.
Students can ask and answer about someone's job and workplace.
meetings.grammarPattern: What does he/she do? Where does he/she work?
meetings.grammarExample: He is a doctor. He works at a hospital.
meetings.grammarNote: Introducing the third-person "does" question form within the familiar simple present tense.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask what job students want to have someday.
Students act out a profession for classmates to guess.
Model the Q&A pattern "What does he/she do? Where does he/she work?".
Students interview a partner about what their parents' jobs are.
Writing 3 sentences about a family member's job and workplace.
A few students share their answers, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct use of "does" in questions and answers.
Written sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Review + Games Day
objectives: Students can review and apply all grammar points from Weeks 1-6.
Students can collaborate effectively in a team game setting.
meetings.grammarExample: I always study on Monday at 8 o'clock. He is a teacher.
meetings.grammarNote: A consolidation session using games rather than new grammar explanation.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, explain today's team game format.
Rapid-fire Q&A recapping frequency, time, and jobs vocabulary.
Briefly review common mistakes noticed across Weeks 1-6.
Teams move around a board game answering grammar questions to advance.
A short combined worksheet reviewing Weeks 1-6.
Announce winning team, closing greeting.

assessment: Team performance in the board game.
Combined review worksheet accuracy.

meetings.title: Places in Town + Prepositions
objectives: Students can name common places in town.
Students can describe locations using in/on/near/between.
meetings.grammarPattern: Where is the...? It is in/on/near/between...
meetings.grammarExample: The hospital is near the park.
meetings.grammarNote: Introducing location prepositions explicitly, building on earlier "where is" question forms.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask what places are near students' homes.
Students act out spatial relationships (near, between) with objects.
Introduce town-place vocabulary and location prepositions with the town map.
In pairs, students describe locations on a shared town map.
Drawing a small town map with at least 5 labeled places.
A few students describe one location on their map, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct use of prepositions describing locations.
Town map labeling accuracy.

meetings.title: Transportation & Simple Directions
objectives: Students can name types of transportation.
Students can give and follow simple directions.
meetings.grammarPattern: How do you go to school? Go straight, turn left/right.
meetings.grammarExample: I go to school by bus. Go straight, then turn left.
meetings.grammarNote: Introducing direction-giving language using the town map from the previous week as context.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask how each student got to school today.
Chanting transportation words with matching movements.
Model asking and giving simple directions using the Week 8 town map.
In pairs, students ask for and give directions using the shared map.
Writing directions from one place to another on their town map.
A few pairs demonstrate their direction roleplay, closing greeting.

assessment: Fluency in the direction-giving roleplay.
Written direction accuracy.

meetings.title: Modals: Can/Can't (Ability)
objectives: Students can express ability and inability using can/can't.
Students can conduct a simple classmate survey about abilities.
meetings.grammarExample: I can swim. I can't fly.
meetings.grammarNote: Explicitly introducing the modal "can" for ability, distinct from ordinary verbs, with its negative form "can't".

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask if anyone can do something unusual.
Quick show-of-hands survey of a few sample abilities.
Explain the modal "can/can't" with example sentences and its fixed form (no -s for he/she).

activities.kegiatan: Practice: What Can You Do? Survey
activities.deskripsi: Students survey 4-5 classmates about their abilities using "Can you...?".
Writing a short paragraph summarizing their survey results.
A few students share one survey result, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct use of can/can't without adding -s.
Survey summary paragraph accuracy.

meetings.title: Modals: Must/Mustn't (Rules)
objectives: Students can express obligation and prohibition using must/mustn't.
Students can create a short set of classroom rules.
meetings.grammarExample: You must wear a helmet. You mustn't run in the hallway.
meetings.grammarNote: Introducing must/mustn't for rules, connected to real situations like school and traffic rules for relevance.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask what rules exist at school.
Sorting picture cards into "good rule" and "broken rule" categories.
Explain must/mustn't with real-life school and traffic rule examples.
In groups, students design a "Classroom Rules" poster using must/mustn't.
Writing 3 personal rules for their own room or house.
Groups briefly present their poster, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct use of must/mustn't in the poster.
Personal rules writing accuracy.

meetings.title: Comparative Adjectives
objectives: Students can form comparative adjectives correctly.
Students can compare two people or objects using a complete sentence.
meetings.grammarExample: Andi is taller than Budi.
meetings.grammarNote: Explicitly teaching the -er/more comparative rule and the "than" structure for comparing two things.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask who is taller between two objects in the room.
Quick oral comparisons of pairs of classroom objects.
Explain comparative formation (-er, more) with the "than" structure on the board.
In pairs, students compare themselves to a partner using 3 comparative sentences.
Writing 5 comparative sentences comparing given picture pairs.
A few students share one comparison, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct comparative formation and use of "than".
Written comparative sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Review + Mini Project: My Neighborhood
objectives: Students can combine places, directions, and comparatives in one project.
Students can present their project confidently to the class.
meetings.grammarExample: The market is near my house. It is bigger than the small shop.
meetings.grammarNote: Consolidating places/prepositions, directions, and comparatives into one connected project, closing Semester 1.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, introduce the "My Neighborhood" project brief.
Students brainstorm places and comparisons to include in their poster.
Review key structures needed: places, prepositions, directions, comparatives.
Students draw and label their neighborhood poster, adding comparative descriptions.
Finalizing poster captions and directions in writing.
A few students present their poster to the class, closing greeting.

assessment: Presentation confidence and clarity.
Correct combined use of places, directions, and comparatives in the poster.

semester2.cp: By the end of Semester 2, students will be able to distinguish present continuous from simple present, talk about hobbies, combine sentences with conjunctions, use superlative adjectives, express future plans with "going to", comprehend short reading texts, conduct WH-question interviews, and write structured descriptive paragraphs, culminating in a final personal-story project.
generalObjectives: Form present continuous sentences and distinguish them from simple present.
Talk about hobbies using the gerund form after like/don't like.
Combine sentences using and, but, and because.
Form superlative adjectives and express future plans with "going to".
Comprehend a short reading text and answer questions about it.
Write a structured paragraph with clear opening, body, and closing sentences.
Combine tenses and structures learned across the year in a final personal story project.
semester2.grammarApproach: Students already master simple present, simple past, and regular/plural nouns, so those are only briefly reviewed as a diagnostic in Week 2. Class time is redirected to new, more challenging structures: adverbs of frequency, modals (can/must), present continuous vs simple present, comparatives & superlatives, conjunctions, and simple future (going to) - each introduced explicitly as a named grammar point, practiced, then produced in speaking or writing.

sessionStructure.deskripsi: Greeting and warm-up question related to the day's topic.
Quick review of the previous session's material or vocabulary.
Explicit introduction of the new grammar point/vocabulary with examples on the board.
Guided speaking/writing practice, games, or roleplay using the new structure.
Independent application: short writing, worksheet, or speaking task.
Recap the grammar point, assign light homework if needed, closing greeting.

petaMateri.grammar: What are you doing? I am...-ing

petaMateri.kosakata: What, Where, When, Who, How, Why, How often

meetings.title: Present Continuous
objectives: Students can form present continuous sentences correctly.
Students can describe an action happening right now.
meetings.grammarPattern: What are you doing? I am ...-ing
meetings.grammarExample: What are you doing? I am reading a book.
meetings.grammarNote: Explicitly introducing present continuous (be + verb-ing) for actions happening now.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, teacher mimes an action and asks "What am I doing?".
Students take turns miming an action for classmates to guess using "-ing".
Explain the present continuous structure (am/is/are + verb-ing) with examples.
Music stops; students freeze in an action pose and describe it in present continuous.
Writing 5 sentences describing pictures of people doing actions.
Recap the be + verb-ing rule, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct formation of present continuous sentences.
Written sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Present Continuous vs Simple Present (Important)
objectives: Students can distinguish habitual actions from actions happening now.
Students can correctly choose between the two tenses in context.
meetings.grammarExample: I play football every day. / I am playing football now.
meetings.grammarNote: This is often a confusing point for students - extra time and a games-based approach are recommended if needed.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask what students usually do vs. what they are doing right now.
Teacher reads sentences; students shout "Now!" or "Always!".
Explain the contrast explicitly with a side-by-side timeline showing habit vs. present moment.
In pairs, students match time-marker cards to the correct tense sentence.
Completing a worksheet choosing the correct tense for each sentence.
Recap the contrast rule with 2 more example sentences, closing greeting.

assessment: Accuracy distinguishing the two tenses in the sentence match-up.
Worksheet accuracy choosing correct tense.

meetings.title: Hobbies & Free Time
objectives: Students can talk about hobbies using simple present plus gerund.
Students can conduct a simple class survey and present results.
meetings.grammarExample: I like swimming. I don't like drawing.
meetings.grammarNote: Introducing the gerund form after "like/don't like", distinct from the present continuous "-ing" just learned.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask students their favorite free-time activity.
Students walk around asking classmates about their hobbies.
Explain the gerund pattern "like/don't like + verb-ing" with examples.
Students survey the class and tally results for a few hobbies.
Drawing a simple bar chart showing the class's favorite hobbies.
A few students present one survey finding, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct gerund use after like/don't like.
Accuracy and clarity of the hobby bar chart.

meetings.title: Conjunctions: and, but, because
objectives: Students can combine two simple sentences using and/but/because.
Students can choose the correct conjunction based on meaning.
meetings.grammarExample: I like rice, but I don't like noodles. I stayed home because it was raining.
meetings.grammarNote: Explicitly teaching three basic conjunctions and the logical relationship each expresses (addition, contrast, reason).

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask students to complete "I like ___ but I don't like ___".
Sorting example sentences by which conjunction fits best.
Explain and/but/because with clear example sentences for each meaning.
In teams, students combine pairs of short sentences using the correct conjunction.
Combining 5 given sentence pairs into one sentence each.
Recap when to use each conjunction, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct conjunction choice in the team race.
Worksheet sentence-combining accuracy.

meetings.title: Superlative Adjectives
objectives: Students can form superlative adjectives correctly.
Students can rank three or more people/objects using superlatives.
meetings.grammarExample: Who is the tallest in class?
meetings.grammarNote: Extending last semester's comparatives to superlatives (-est/most) for comparing three or more items.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask who is the tallest person in the room.
Quickly ranking 3 classroom objects from biggest to smallest.
Explain superlative formation (-est, most) with example sentences on the board.
Students rank classmates or objects and describe them using superlatives.
Writing 5 superlative sentences based on given picture sets.
A few students share one superlative sentence, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct superlative formation.
Written sentence accuracy.

meetings.title: Simple Future: Going to
objectives: Students can express future plans using "going to".
Students can describe their weekend plans in a short spoken text.
meetings.grammarExample: I am going to visit my grandmother this weekend.
meetings.grammarNote: Introducing "going to" for pre-decided future plans, distinct from present continuous which was studied earlier.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask what students usually do on weekends.
Sorting sentences into "habit" (simple present) vs "plan" (going to).
Explain the "going to" structure with clear example sentences.
In pairs, students interview each other about weekend plans using "going to".
Writing a short paragraph about their weekend plan.
A few students share their weekend plan, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct use of "going to" for future plans.
Weekend plan paragraph accuracy.

meetings.title: Review + Games Day
objectives: Students can review and apply grammar points from Weeks 14-19.
Students can collaborate effectively in a team guessing game.
meetings.grammarExample: I am playing now, but I usually study. I am going to visit my cousin.
meetings.grammarNote: A consolidation session using games rather than new grammar explanation.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, explain today's team game format.
Rapid-fire Q&A recapping present continuous, hobbies, and conjunctions.
Briefly review common mistakes noticed across Weeks 14-19.
Teams take turns describing a word for teammates to guess without saying it.
A short combined worksheet reviewing Weeks 14-19.
Announce winning team, closing greeting.

assessment: Team performance in the guessing game.
Combined review worksheet accuracy.

meetings.title: Reading Comprehension
objectives: Students can read a short mixed-tense story and understand its main events.
Students can answer comprehension questions about a short text.
meetings.grammarPattern: Comprehension of mixed tenses in context
meetings.grammarExample: Read a short story (6-8 sentences) and answer questions.
meetings.grammarNote: Applying previously learned tenses receptively through reading, rather than teaching new grammar.
vocab: Vocabulary drawn from the reading text

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, predict the story topic from its picture.
Looking at story illustrations and guessing what happens.
Read the short story aloud together, pausing to check understanding.
In pairs, students discuss and answer oral comprehension questions.
Completing written comprehension questions about the story.
Recap the story's main events together, closing greeting.

assessment: Understanding shown through discussion answers.
Written comprehension question accuracy.

meetings.title: WH-Questions & Interview
objectives: Students can form questions using all WH-question words.
Students can conduct and report back a short interview.
meetings.grammarPattern: What, Where, When, Who, How, Why, How often + verb
meetings.grammarExample: Where do you live? How often do you read?
meetings.grammarNote: Consolidating all WH-question words together in one structured interview task.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, quick review of WH-question words with a matching game.
Matching each WH-word to its meaning/example question.
Model a short interview using a range of WH-questions.
Students interview a partner using at least 5 different WH-questions.
Writing a short report of their partner's interview answers.
A few students report one interview finding, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct formation of varied WH-questions.
Interview report accuracy and clarity.

meetings.title: Writing: Paragraph Structure
objectives: Students can identify opening, body, and closing sentences in a paragraph.
Students can write a 5-6 sentence paragraph with clear structure.
meetings.grammarExample: My family is small. We live in a big house. We are very happy.
meetings.grammarNote: Explicitly teaching paragraph structure as a writing skill, using descriptive adjectives learned earlier.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, read a simple model paragraph together.
Identifying the opening, body, and closing sentences in the model paragraph.
Explain paragraph structure using the graphic organizer.
As a class, build a paragraph together about the classroom step by step.
Writing their own 5-6 sentence paragraph about their family or room.
A few students read one sentence from their paragraph, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct identification of paragraph parts.
Clarity and structure of the written paragraph.

meetings.title: Descriptive Writing (Continued)
objectives: Students can describe an object or person in more vivid detail.
Students can order adjectives correctly in a simple description.
meetings.grammarExample: It is a small, red bag. She is a tall, friendly girl.
meetings.grammarNote: Building on Week 23's paragraph skills by focusing on simple adjective ordering within descriptions.

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, describe a classroom object using 2 adjectives.
Practicing simple adjective order with quick example pairs.
Explain simple adjective ordering with example descriptions.
In pairs, students describe a picture prompt in as much detail as possible.
Writing a detailed description paragraph of a person or object.
A few students share one description, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct simple adjective ordering.
Detail and accuracy of the written description.

meetings.title: Conversation Practice
objectives: Students can use everyday expressions in common social situations.
Students can perform a short roleplay dialogue confidently.
meetings.grammarExample: Can I have a burger, please? / Hello, may I speak to Rani?
meetings.grammarNote: Applying the year's grammar and vocabulary in realistic everyday conversation contexts.
vocab: everyday expressions (May I..., Can I..., Excuse me)
media: Roleplay scenario cards (shop, phone call, restaurant)

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, ask when students last used polite English phrases.
Matching common expressions to the situation they're used in.
Model each roleplay scenario (shop, phone, restaurant) briefly.
In pairs, students rotate through 2-3 different roleplay scenario cards.
Writing out one roleplay dialogue they performed.
A few pairs perform their favorite roleplay, closing greeting.

assessment: Fluency and confidence across roleplay scenarios.
Written dialogue accuracy.

meetings.title: Review Akhir + Final Project: My Story
objectives: Students can combine tenses and structures learned across the whole year in one connected text.
Students can present their final project confidently to the class.
meetings.grammarPattern: Combination of all structures learned this year
meetings.grammarExample: I am 10 years old. I live in Bekasi. Every day I go to school. Last week I visited my grandmother. Next month I am going to join a competition.
meetings.grammarNote: The capstone task of the year, consolidating simple present, simple past, present continuous, modals, comparatives, conjunctions, and future "going to" into one personal story.
vocab: Review vocabulary from the whole year

activities.deskripsi: Greeting, introduce the "My Story" final project brief.
Students brainstorm key facts about themselves, past events, and future plans.
Review which tense/structure fits each part of a personal story (now, past, future).
Students draft their "My Story" text combining several tenses and structures.
Finalizing and decorating their "My Story" project page.
A few students present their final project to the class, closing greeting.

assessment: Correct and varied use of the year's grammar structures in the story.
Presentation confidence for the final project.
